aka: The Teaching of the Twelve Apostles
intro: A brief manual of early Christian instruction covering moral teaching, baptism, prayer, the Eucharist, and the leadership of local communities. It is one of the oldest surviving Christian writings outside the New Testament.

facts.label: Authorship
facts.value: Anonymous; presented as the teaching of the Twelve Apostles

facts.label: Place of origin
facts.value: Uncertain; Syria or Palestine are often proposed

facts.label: Canonical status
facts.value: Not part of the New Testament canon; valued by some early writers for instruction

background.text: The Didache is a short work of sixteen chapters. It opens with moral instruction framed as a choice between two ways, one of life and one of death, then gives directions for baptism, fasting, prayer, and the Eucharist, and closes with guidance on traveling teachers, local leaders, and watchfulness for the last days.

For centuries the work was known only from mentions by other writers. A complete Greek text was rediscovered in 1873 by Philotheos Bryennios in a manuscript held in Constantinople and published in 1883.
Many scholars regard the Didache as a composite work assembled from earlier traditions, including a "Two Ways" teaching that also appears in the Epistle of Barnabas.
Its relationship to the Gospel of Matthew, with which it shares the Lord's Prayer and several sayings, remains debated. It may draw on Matthew, on shared oral tradition, or on both.

structure.title: Baptism, fasting, prayer, and the Eucharist
